task_instruction: The reference material above is a pre-meeting brief for this call, built only from the call's own published participant roster and press-release documents: participants and their roles, the organizations and divisions the roster names, company and ticker candidates, product and segment candidates, and other document terms. Where an entry shows a form in brackets after "normalized:", that is the spelling the measurement compares against. Below it, a first-pass transcript of this same audio window is given. Return that first-pass transcript again, word for word, changing it ONLY where the audio and the reference material together show that a named entity -- a person, organization, place, product, event or other proper name -- is spelled or identified wrongly; replace the wrong name with the right one in place. Do not add words, do not remove words, do not re-order or re-punctuate, and do not change any word that is not part of a name. Never insert a listed word you do not clearly hear in the audio. If nothing needs correcting, return the transcript unchanged. Output only the transcript text.
what_this_is: configs/baseline/e21-kc-e1f-brief-repair.json -- the ADMITTED (provisional) substitution-only repair arm -- with THREE functional keys added and NONE changed. Every other value is byte for byte KC-E1f's, so the arm, the policy, the evidence source, the brief cap, the predecessor binding, the repair frame, the delivery rule and its three parameters, the task instruction, the scorers, the OBS protocol and the batch geometry are that cell's. The single factor is the REVIEWER PLUS THE SELECTIVE RE-LISTEN: instead of one contact per 90-second window carrying the whole window's audio and the whole window's pass-1 text, the hash-pinned selective plan gives ONE contact per FLAGGED window, carrying a re-cut of that window widened by a 5.0-second context margin on each side and floored at 10.0 seconds, with the matching half-open range of that window's own pass-1 words. An unflagged window is never contacted and delivers its predecessor verbatim.
why_window_review_and_window_observe_are: They are not consumed at run time -- the pinned plan already fixes every position, which is what makes slice batching legal -- but they are not decoration either: the wire check asserts that every value here EQUALS the plan document's own flag_source, context_margin_seconds, min_relisten_seconds and judge list, so a fragment that claims one Reviewer and pins a plan built by another is refused before any contact. The judge ids additionally resolve in core.base.JUDGES through scripts/checks/engineering_base_check.py's any-depth 'judges' rule, exactly as a phase_review block's do.
on_flag_vocabulary_note: 'recut-and-contact' is this fragment's own word for what the plan encodes and is NOT rails.phase_review's on_flag vocabulary, whose 'loop' value stays refused by name. Nothing loops here: the criticism is computed once, model-free, on a sealed draft, and what it decides is which windows are CONTACTED AT ALL -- a selection made before the first request, never a re-ask after one.
why_the_repair_frame_is_unchanged: e21-entity-repair-frame-v1 says 'First-pass transcript of this same audio window'. Under a re-listen the audio window the core receives IS the re-cut, and the text it is shown is that re-cut's own pass-1 words, so the sentence stays true and the frame stays frozen. Minting a second frame would have added a factor the cell does not intend to move.
why_the_delivery_parameters_are_unchange: min_anchor_ratio 0.6 and max_substituted_fraction 0.1 are RATIOS, and the unit they are computed over moves from the whole 90-second window to the re-cut span. That is a consequence of the factor, not a second factor: the rule is byte-identical and its relative strictness is unchanged. In absolute terms it becomes tighter per contact -- roughly two substituted tokens on a twenty-five-word span where a hundred-and-eighty-word window allowed eighteen -- which is reported as a covariate, never tuned.
plan_pin_basis: obs_unit_plan_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the committed plan file and the seam refuses to load bytes that disagree with it. The plan is model-free (exposure row SAEA-E21-MF-LOOP-1-PREP-V1): it was built by scripts/build_e21_relisten_plan.py from the sealed comparator's own per-window drafts, the ConEC participant rosters through the registered reader, and the two registered gold-free judges -- no reference transcript, no wer_tags sidecar and no score file. Its loader re-proves, per call and on the bytes actually loaded, that every unit lies inside its named parent window, clears the refusal-to-shrink floor, names a non-empty word range inside that window's own pass-1 text, and that the units are one per flagged window in ascending order.
why_the_window_keys_stay: obs_buffer_seconds 90 and the advance keys are left at KC-E1f's values rather than removed. Under a plan they are inert, and deleting them would make this fragment differ from the arm it is measured against in keys the cell does not vary. obs_buffer_seconds also remains the cap every re-cut was built under, so the two numbers cannot silently disagree. obs_boundary_mode stays 'fixed' because the plan fixes every position before the first contact, which is the independence condition slice batching requires.
composes_but_is_not_permission: This fragment composing is not a GO. E21-LOOP-1 needs its own exposure row and the owner's authorization to fly, and neither is granted by this file. Owner Decision 12-G of 2026-09-08 authorized the MODEL-FREE preparation only, and the cell flies after the SLURP line.
